npcs.name: Fiona the Harper
npcs.idle: Lorcan wrote me a poem every day for a year. Then he wrote them for someone else.

npcs.name: Turf-Reeve Fergal
npcs.idle: Siopa's a fort and a turf-yard. The turf keeps Alainn Bin warm. The road keeps the turf moving. The road is my whole job.

npcs.name: Tomas the Peat-Cutter
npcs.idle: Thirty years cutting turf. You find things. Bog butter. A boot. Last week, a gold collar the size of my head.

npcs.name: Old Sadhbh
npcs.idle: I've keened for three chieftains. The banshee keened first, every time.

npcs.name: Steward Conn
npcs.idle: The Chieftess is well. Perfectly well. Please don't trouble her.

npcs.name: Captain Ruairc
npcs.idle: The Chieftess holds Alainn Bin. I hold everything she can see from her window. Lately, that's less.

npcs.name: Keener Brid
npcs.idle: We keen for the dead. Lately we read the lights too. A Keener has to know which lights mean a death.

quests.title: The Siopa Road
quests.offer:
The siabra have put a post on the Siopa road - wayguards and their hounds, right across it. No turf's gone to Alainn Bin in a week.

The odd thing: the siabra used to rob the road. Now they just stand on it and turn people back. As if they're keeping it clear for something. Will you [clear the post]?
quests.summary: A siabra wayguard post on the Siopa road turns everyone back.

steps.goal: Clear the siabra wayguard post about 290 m north-east of Turf-Reeve Fergal
Search the wayguard post

clue.name: siabra orders, scratched on a glowing slate

steps.text: A slate that glows, scratched with siabra marks. Fergal will want to see it: it's a map of the bog with lines drawn from the tower in the middle out to every road.

steps.goal: Bring the slate to Turf-Reeve Fergal
steps.say:
Lines from the Gemstone Tower to every road. They're not keeping the roads clear. They're keeping them dark - so whatever walks out of that tower at night can walk where it likes.

The Clann at Alainn Bin should see this. Captain Ruairc.

quests.title: The Cullen Gold
quests.offer:
You heard about the collar? Everyone has. The siabra too, it seems - they've come for it twice, and for me with it.

I've buried it again, out in the cuttings. Will you [stand by me] while I dig it up and get it to Alainn Bin? The Chieftess can keep it. I don't want it.
quests.summary: Tomas the Peat-Cutter found a gold collar in the turf, and the siabra want it.

steps.goal: Keep Tomas alive while he digs up the gold about 0 m east of Tomas the Peat-Cutter
steps.text: Tomas lifts the collar out of the turf. Even in daylight it glows faintly - and he swears it didn't, last week.

stages.name: Keep Tomas alive
stages.announce: Tomas starts to dig. Out of the reeds come siabra raiders, running low.

steps.goal: Take Tomas and the gold to Captain Ruairc in Alainn Bin
steps.say:
The Cullen gold. The old kings' hoard - there's more of it under that turf than in Tara.

And it glows. Everything out there glows lately. Fergal's slate says the tower. I say the siabra serve something in that tower, and it wants gold - or light, or both.

quests.title: The Post-Captains
quests.offer:
Two siabra posts hold the north-west marches - Muroi's and Enan's. Their captains take orders from the tower and pass them on.

Will you [break the posts]? Kill the captains. I want their seals.
quests.summary: Captain Ruairc wants the siabra post-captains Muroi and Enan dead.

steps.goal: Kill Muroi, who holds the western siabra post about 1.4 km north-west of Captain Ruairc
Kill Enan, who holds the northern siabra post
steps.text: Enan's seal glows. Pressed to wax, it shows a crown of light - not a siabra mark at all.

steps.goal: Bring the seals to Captain Ruairc
steps.say:
A crown of light. The Glimmer King's mark - the Azure crusaders on the north road wear it on their banners, crossed out.

So the siabra have a new king. One causeway left between the marches and the tower: Saemus holds it.

quests.title: The Causeway
quests.offer:
The causeway runs from the north marches into the middle of the bog, toward the tower. Saemus holds it with waterwalkers.

And Fergal says there are poles along it, in a line, every forty paces - like lamp-posts. Will you [take the causeway]?
quests.summary: Saemus and his waterwalkers hold the causeway to the tower, and there are poles along it like lamp-posts.

steps.goal: Kill the siabra waterwalkers on the causeway about 1.0 km north-west of Captain Ruairc
Kill Saemus at the head of the causeway
Look at the poles along the causeway

clue.name: a lantern-pole, hung with a glowing bead

steps.text: Each pole carries a bead of glass with a light in it, and the lights lean toward the tower like flowers toward the sun. A road of lights, for walking on the bog at night.

steps.goal: Report to Captain Ruairc
steps.say:
A road of lights. The siabra built a lit road from the marches to the tower. For whom?

The Keeners will have a word for it. Old Sadhbh, or Brid. Me, I just want to burn it.

quests.title: Pages in the Reeds
quests.offer:
Pages. Lorcan's verse, stuck to the reeds all over the bog - and at night, Keener Brid says, they glow.

Before I ask anything else of you, will you [gather the pages]? I want to read what he's writing. Even if it's for her.
quests.summary: Pages of Lorcan's verse are stuck to the reeds all over the bog, and they glow at night.

steps.goal: Gather the glowing pages from the reeds by the causeway about 360 m north-east of Fiona the Harper
steps.text: Lorcan's verse, in an old man's hand. Every line is about light: light on water, light in a tower, light that takes away weeping.

steps.goal: Put out the bog lights circling the pages
Bring the pages to Fiona
steps.say:
He never wrote about light. He wrote about me, and rain, and his mother's kitchen. This is someone else's song in his hand.

The lhiannan-sidhe is a muse. Something is singing through her. Bring him [home] - whatever it takes.

quests.title: The Lhiannan-Sidhe
quests.offer:
Lorcan was my lover and the finest poet in Cullen. Last spring a lhiannan-sidhe found him - a faerie muse. They give a poet the best verses he'll ever write, and they drink his life to do it.

He wrote to me last month, from somewhere in the bog. The writing was an old man's. He's thirty. Will you [find Lorcan]?
quests.summary: A lhiannan-sidhe - a faerie muse who feeds on poets - has taken Fiona's lover into the bog.

steps.goal: Go into the bog by the siabra causeway
steps.text: Siabra watch from the posts. Pages of verse are stuck to the reeds, soaked, the ink running.

steps.goal: Fight through the siabra wayguards
Gather the scattered verses

clue.name: pages of verse in a shaking hand

steps.text: Each page better than the last, and each hand older. The last pages are nearly illegible - and nearly perfect.

steps.goal: Cut through the bog creepers to the east
Find Lorcan
steps.say:
Fiona sent you. Fiona. I wrote her a hundred poems and none of them were good enough. Now I write for HER, and every one is perfect - she brings the light, and the light brings the words.

She'll come at dusk. Look at me. I'm thirty. I don't care. Do you understand - every [word]...

steps.goal: Drive off the lhiannan-sidhe
steps.text: The lhiannan-sidhe falls back, hissing, into the mist, and the light goes with her. Lorcan clutches his chest and breathes like a man surfacing from deep water.

stages.name: the Lhiannan-Sidhe
stages.announce: A woman more beautiful than the moon walks out of the mist, lit from inside. 'He is mine. He is my masterpiece. The light says so.'

steps.goal: Decide what becomes of the verses
steps.say:
She's not gone. Not while I have the verses. They're hers as much as mine - she lives in them. If I [burn the verses], I'm free, and I'll go back to Fiona and write bad poems and grow old slowly.

If I [keep them], she'll come back, and I'll die before winter, and they'll sing these in every hall in Hibernia for a thousand years. Choose. Please. I can't.

options.say: ...They burn so slowly. ...There. I can't remember a line. Not one. Take me to Fiona.
Then I'll keep them. Tell Fiona the best ones are hers. They are. Tell her I'm sorry.

steps.goal: Return to Fiona
steps.say: He's home. He's grey and thin and he can't remember a word he wrote - and he wrote me a poem this morning. It's terrible. It's the best thing I've ever read.

steps.goal: Return to Fiona
steps.say:
He kept them. And he sent me the best ones.

They're... they're beyond anything. I'll set them to music. I'll play them at his wake, which will be before winter. Take this, and go, before I cry on you.

burned.text: Take this. He wanted you to.

quests.title: Where the Muses Go
quests.offer:
Fiona's muse isn't the only one. There are lhiannan-sidhe all over the bog this year, and they all sing the same song now - light, light, light. They've found a better patron than poets.

Will you [silence them]? The two that sing loudest are in the reeds by the tower and east of it.
quests.summary: The lhiannan-sidhe of the bog all sing the Glimmer's song now.

steps.goal: Silence the lhiannan-sidhe in the reeds by the causeway about 820 m north-west of Keener Brid
Silence the lhiannan-sidhe east of the tower
steps.text: With her last breath she sings one line clear: 'The lantern-bearer keeps the light, the light keeps the tower, the tower keeps the bog.'

steps.goal: Report to Keener Brid
steps.say:
The lantern-bearer. In the tower.

Sadhbh needs to hear this - but not now. Now she's listening to the banshee, and the banshee is keening for the Chieftess.

quests.title: The Keen
quests.offer:
Listen. Do you hear it? No - you wouldn't, yet. The banshee of Cullen. She keens on her stone in the bog north of town, for a death in the old families.

The black wraiths have gathered round her stone. Will you [go to the stone]? Clear them away. I want to hear her plain.
quests.summary: The banshee of Cullen keens on her stone north of Alainn Bin, and the black wraiths have gathered round it.

steps.goal: Clear the black wraiths round the keening stones about 300 m west of Old Sadhbh
Stand by the keening stone and listen
steps.text: Far off, a woman keening. And another, nearer, keening wrong - too high, too bright, like a voice through glass.

steps.goal: Report to Old Sadhbh
steps.say:
Two keeners. One's the banshee of Cullen; I'd know her anywhere. The other's false. Riolda - a banshee that walked into the lights, and keens for whatever they tell her to.

And the true one keens for the Chieftess. Who isn't sick.

quests.title: Riolda
quests.offer:
Riolda. A banshee who keens false. She walks the keening ground at night, and wherever she keens, the bog-lights come.

She'll drown the true keen in hers, and then nobody will know whose death is coming. Will you [silence Riolda]? Only at night. She's not there by day.
quests.summary: Riolda, a banshee who walked into the lights, keens false on the keening ground at night.

steps.goal: Silence Riolda on the keening ground (at night) about 230 m west of Old Sadhbh
steps.text: Riolda's keen breaks off. In the silence, clear and far, the true banshee: keening for the Chieftess, and under it a name. Conn.

steps.goal: Report to Old Sadhbh
steps.say:
Conn. The steward.

Twenty years he's served her. ...Look in his room, before I say a word to anyone. Find me proof.

quests.title: The Steward's Letters
quests.offer:
Conn's room is in the Chieftess' hall, and he locks it. He keeps his papers in a box under the floor; the maids know, maids always know.

Will you [search his room] while he's at the market? Quietly.
quests.summary: Old Sadhbh wants Steward Conn's hidden papers found.

steps.goal: Search under the floor of Steward Conn's room about 20 m south-east of Old Sadhbh

clue.name: a box of letters sealed in blue wax

steps.text: Letters sealed in blue wax - the Order of the Azure's. 'When the Chieftess is gone, your son will hold Alainn Bin, and Alainn Bin will open its gates to the Order and its torches. The bog must burn. Payment enclosed.' And a purse of Azure silver.

steps.goal: Bring the letters to Old Sadhbh
steps.say:
The Azure. The Azure paid him.

They want the Chieftess dead so they can burn the bog - with the turf-cutters, and Siopa, and us, if we're in the way. Because of the lights.

Right. Now we stop it. Properly. Bring friends.

quests.title: The Keening
quests.offer:
This is GROUP work, so bring friends you trust.

The banshee of Cullen has keened under the Chieftess' window every night for a week. The letters say why: Conn poisons her for the Azure. But a poisoner never trusts poison alone.

Will you [find out who] waits to finish it? Start with the [steward]. Let him think we know nothing.

topics.steward: Conn. He runs the Chieftess' household. He's very calm. Far too calm.

quests.summary: GROUP. The banshee of Cullen keens nightly for the Chieftess. Steward Conn poisons her for the Azure - and someone waits to finish it.

steps.goal: Question Steward Conn
steps.say:
The banshee? Old women's stories. The Chieftess is perfectly well. I see to everything - her food, her wine, her guests. I'd know if anything were wrong.

If you must poke about, the black wraiths in the bog to the [east] have been bold of late. Go and deal with them. That would actually be useful.

steps.goal: Deal with the black wraiths east of town
steps.text: Among the wraith-mud, a dropped satchel - a steward's satchel, with a steward's seal.

steps.goal: Search the dropped satchel
steps.text: A vial of sidhe glass, nearly empty. A letter: 'Half in her wine each night. By the dark moon it will look like a wasting. The venator will finish it if it doesn't. - C.'

steps.goal: Find the banshee's keening-stone
steps.text: A grey woman sits on a stone in the bog, combing her hair, weeping. She looks up at you.

steps.goal: Speak with the banshee
steps.say:
You hear me. Good. Few do, before.

The Chieftess' death is close. The steward pours it. And the siabra hunter waits in the bog to the west of my stone, to finish it if the poison is slow - bought with Azure silver, though siabra and Azure hate each other. Stop the [hunter]. I am so tired of keening.

steps.goal: Kill the siabra assassin in the bog
steps.text: The venator dies in the bog-water. Far off, under the Chieftess' window, the keening stops.

stages.name: Iuchra the Venator
stages.announce: A siabra in mud-grey leathers rises out of the bog with a knife in each hand. 'The steward pays well. You'll do for practice.'

steps.goal: Return to Old Sadhbh
steps.say:
The keening's stopped. I heard it stop at moonrise. And you have the vial. Conn.

Conn, who has served her twenty years. He wanted the chieftainship for his son, and the Azure promised it.

The Chieftess is too kind. She'll want to [banish him]. The old law says [death] for a poisoner. She'll ask me, and I'll ask you. You've seen more of it than I have.

options.say: Banished. Beyond the Shannon, with nothing but his cloak. ...She'll weep for him. She's like that.
The old law, then. I'll keen for him myself. Somebody should.

banished.text: From the Chieftess, with her thanks.

quests.title: The Azure March
quests.offer:
The Order of the Azure has come down the north road from the Sheeroe Hills. Crusaders, cleansers, banners with a crown crossed out. They say they're here for the lights.

They're burning turf-cutters' huts as they come. Will you [stop the march]? The north road, before they reach the cuttings.
quests.summary: The Order of the Azure marches down the north road, burning turf-cutters' huts.

steps.goal: Break the Azure crusaders on the north road about 1.0 km north of Captain Ruairc
Report to Captain Ruairc
steps.say: They fight like men who've already won. ...The Glimmer took the Sheeroe Hills from them. They mean to burn the bog to keep it from taking this too, and they don't much care who's standing on it.

quests.title: The Pyre
quests.offer:
The Azure have built a pyre on the north edge of the bog - barrels of pitch, and their banishers praying over it. When it's lit, the fire goes into the peat, and peat burns for years. Underground. The whole bog.

Will you [break the pyre]? Kill the banishers. Spill the pitch into the water.
quests.summary: The Azure have built a pyre of pitch on the bog's north edge - lit, it would set the peat burning for years.

steps.goal: Kill the azure banishers at the pyre about 1.0 km north of Captain Ruairc
Spill the pitch barrels into the bog
steps.text: The pitch glugs out into the black water and lies there. On the barrels, an order: 'Marshal Cathbarr: when the steward's work is done, fire the bog from the north. Alainn Bin will open its gates.'

steps.goal: Report to Captain Ruairc
steps.say:
'When the steward's work is done.' Conn. The Keeners were right.

Marshal Cathbarr. He sits in the Azure camp on the north road with his banners. One more push and we go for him.

quests.title: The Cleansers
quests.offer:
Before we go for Cathbarr: his cleansers and idolaters are out in the eastern bog, hunting siabra and burning the reeds. The bears are fleeing into the turf-cutters' camps.

Will you [thin them]? Cleansers and idolaters. Then we go.
quests.summary: The Azure's cleansers and idolaters are burning the reeds of the eastern bog.

steps.goal: Kill the azure cleansers burning the reeds about 900 m north of Captain Ruairc
Kill the azure idolaters
steps.text: Overhead, a black crow, bigger than an eagle, circling the smoke. Badb. The battle-crow came down when the burning started.

steps.goal: Report to Captain Ruairc
steps.say:
Badb. If she's circling, the fighting's not over. She always knows.

Right. Cathbarr. Bring friends.

quests.title: Marshal Cathbarr
quests.offer:
GROUP work.

Marshal Cathbarr of the Order of the Azure, in his camp on the north road, with his banners and his crusaders. He paid a steward to poison a chieftess so he could burn the bog.

We go in, we break him, the Azure go back to the hills. Say [for Alainn Bin] when your friends are ready.
quests.summary: GROUP. Break Marshal Cathbarr of the Azure in his camp on the north road.

steps.goal: Gather below the Azure camp on the north road about 1.0 km north of Captain Ruairc
steps.text: Blue banners with the crown crossed out. Somewhere a man is preaching about fire.

steps.goal: Defeat Marshal Cathbarr in the Azure camp
steps.text: Cathbarr falls among his banners. 'You'll wish we'd burned it,' he says. 'When the Glimmer King comes down out of the hills - you'll wish.' Above, the great crow circles once, and goes back to her mound.

stages.name: Marshal Cathbarr
stages.announce: A tall man in blue enamel turns from his pyre-plans. 'Lantern-lovers. The Glimmer will thank you. Then it'll take your eyes.'

steps.goal: Report to Captain Ruairc
steps.say:
The Azure are pulling back up the north road. Some of them - the young ones - want to stay. They say they hate the Glimmer as much as we do, and they're not wrong.

We could [take them in], under the Clann's eye. Or we [send them north] with the rest. Your call. You broke their marshal.

options.say: Then they stay. Under the Clann's eye, and no torches. ...We'll see if a crusader can learn to cut turf.
North, then. Every one. Let the Order keep its zealots.

taken.text: From the Clann of Alainn Bin.

sent.text: From the Clann of Alainn Bin.

quests.title: Reading the Lights
quests.offer:
The bog-lights - the will-o'-the-wisps that lead travellers off the path. Every Keener reads them: a light over the water means a death. This year they all come from one place, and they all go back to it.

Will you [hunt the bog-lights] at night? I want to see what they carry back.
quests.summary: The bog-lights all come from the Gemstone Tower and go back to it.

steps.goal: Put out the bog-lights near the tower, at night about 640 m north-west of Keener Brid
steps.text: Each light, as it goes out, drops something: a speck of bright stone, like a chip off a gem.

steps.goal: Bring the bright chips to Keener Brid
steps.say:
Gem-chips. From the Gemstone Tower's walls. The lights are pieces of the tower walking about.

The tower was Cliodna's, the northern queen's - she left it this spring. Something else moved in, and the gems in the walls answer to it now.

quests.title: The Three Gems
quests.offer:
Three great gems in the tower's walls - green, white and red. The old tales say Cliodna set them there to watch the bog. Now they shine.

Will you [look at the gems]? Get close. The wards at the gate will try to stop you.
quests.summary: The three great gems in the Gemstone Tower's walls shine with the Glimmer's light.

steps.goal: Kill the glimmer wards at the tower gate about 470 m north-west of Keener Brid
Look at the great gems in the tower's walls
steps.text: Green, white and red, each as big as a head, each blazing. Inside each, like a fly in amber, a little shape of light: a crowned man. Watching the bog.

steps.goal: Report to Keener Brid
steps.say:
A crowned man. Cuuldurach - the Glimmer King, the dragon in the Sheeroe Hills. He's looking out of Cliodna's gems.

Break the gems and he's blind here. But they're kept, and the keeper is the lantern-bearer the muses sang about. That's for many hands. And Badb - Badb sits on her mound by the gate, and nothing passes her when she's hungry.

quests.title: The Crow on the Mound
quests.offer:
GROUP work - real war-band work.

Badb. The battle-crow, the war-goddess's sister. She's come down on the mound by the tower because she smells war, and she's right: Azure, Glimmer, siabra, us. She feeds on it. While she sits there nobody reaches the tower gate.

Will you [face Badb]? Bring everyone. A Keener will keen for whoever she takes.
quests.summary: GROUP. Badb, the battle-crow, sits on her mound by the Gemstone Tower and feeds on the war.

steps.goal: Defeat Badb, the battle-crow, on her mound by the tower about 750 m north-west of Old Sadhbh
steps.text: Badb comes down out of the air as a woman, and stands, and laughs. 'Well fought. I'll come back when you've a better war.' Then she is a crow again, and gone.

steps.goal: Report to Old Sadhbh
steps.say:
She'll be back. She always is. But not for a while.

The gate's open. Brid's waiting.

quests.title: The Lantern-Bearer
quests.offer:
GROUP work, the last of it here.

The lantern-bearer keeps the light, the light keeps the tower, the tower keeps the bog. Kill the keeper and the gems go dark, and Cuuldurach is blind in Cullen.

Say [into the tower] when your friends are ready.
quests.summary: GROUP. The Glimmer's lantern-bearer keeps the light at the top of the Gemstone Tower.

steps.goal: Climb into the Gemstone Tower about 450 m north-west of Keener Brid
steps.text: The walls are warm. The great gems blaze. Somewhere above, someone is humming a song you've heard in Lough Gur.

steps.goal: Defeat the Glimmer's lantern-bearer at the top of the tower
steps.text: The lantern-bearer's lamp cracks, and one by one the great gems go dark - green, white, red. Out over the bog, every light goes out at once.

stages.name: Lochru the Lantern-Bearer
stages.announce: A tall shape of light lifts a lamp. 'You put out a herald on a lake. You will not put out the King's own lantern.'

steps.goal: Report to Keener Brid
steps.say:
Dark. The whole bog, dark, the way it should be at night. I could weep.

The tower is ours now - the Keeners'. We could [break the gems] so nothing can ever look through them again. Or we [keep the gems] and learn to look back through them - north, into the Sheeroe Hills, at him.

options.say: Broken, then. Nobody looks through Cliodna's eyes again. Nobody.
Kept. And one night soon a Keener will look north through the red one - and the Glimmer King will look back.
